title: Streaming envelope + checksum + idempotent-toolcall recovery
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Streaming structured JSON responses plus tool/function calls are exposing brittle failure modes when chunks truncate mid-object or mid-toolcall. Legacy clients expect newline-delimited JSON; newer clients expect a framed envelope. We need a protocol and server-side repair path that preserves ordered delivery, enables idempotent tool call semantics, and remains backward-compatible with older SDKs.

Proposal: 1) Emit a lightweight stream envelope header per chunk: {seq:int, token_anchor:int, payload_len:int, crc32:string, tool_call_id?:string}. The header is encoded as a single-line JSON followed by a 0x1E (RS) record separator, then the raw byte payload. This lets clients detect corruption/truncation and attempt deterministic repairs.

2) Checksum & token anchoring: Server calculates crc32 over the payload bytes and includes token_anchor at a token boundary approximation (byte offset or token index when available). On reconnect, clients present last-seen seq + token_anchor; server attempts to resume from nearest cache checkpoint.

3) Idempotent tool calls: When a model emits a tool/function call, attach tool_call_id that is globally unique per call (UUID v4) and persist transient metadata in the runtime until the call is acknowledged. If a client retries because of truncation, the runtime will de-duplicate by tool_call_id. For older clients that lack tool_call_id, fall back to content hashing + token_anchor heuristics.

4) Truncation repair heuristics: If crc mismatch or missing bytes are detected, apply graded strategies: a) request byte-range replay from server using seq numbers, b) if replay not feasible, synthesize best-effort JSON repair using bracket matching on last N KB plus escape normalization, c) escalate to full-response re-generation with lightweight rerun constraints (same seed, model variant).

5) Compatibility layer: Server supports three modes per route: legacy (newline-delimited JSON only), framed (envelope+RS), and auto (try framed, fall back to legacy). SDKs will expose auto by default. Console and observability will decode envelopes for telemetry and show per-seq CRC/pass-fail stats.

Implementation notes: Add streamed-envelope encoder/decoder in runtime and SDKs, store minimal per-stream metadata in in-memory shard for 60s, extend trace/span to include seq/checksum/tool_call_id. Add unit/integration tests that fuzz partial-chunk boundaries and validate idempotency for toolcall flows.

Acceptance criteria: - New encoder in runtime with feature-flag enabled on a percentage of traffic - SDKs (node + python) can decode envelope and recover by requesting replay for missing sequences - No observable increase in 99th percentile tail latency >3% in Dedicated clusters - E2E tests for tool idempotency pass under simulated truncation and reconnects.
comments: 2026-03-02: Kickoff sync with RD, infra, SDKs. Agreed on RS (0x1E) separator to minimize collateral breakage with newline-based parsers. - Aisha
2026-03-03: Prototype encoder in go-runtime completed. Emits header line + RS + payload. Basic decoder in python SDK passes happy-path. - Miguel
2026-03-04: Design feedback from DX: include human-readable seq in header for easier debugging in Console. Added seq field. Also requested explicit tool_call_id field. - Lena (DX)

2026-03-06: Infra raised concern about memory retention for per-stream metadata at scale. Decided to cap in-memory retention to 60s and evict LRU. Miguel to follow up with evict metrics. - Priya (Infra)

2026-03-08: Implemented CRC32 checksum and token_anchor heuristics. Found case where token_anchor is approximate for subword tokenization; we will expose both token_index (optional) and byte_offset. - Miguel
2026-03-09: Added end-to-end fuzz tests that drop random bytes at chunk boundary. Repair heuristics recovered valid JSON in 92/100 runs; failures tracked in ENG-96128. - QA
